turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm Owen's mother, and I have about twenty minutes. Who decided that Owen's essay was a zero, and when did they decide it?
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Words are cheap, Hale. The zero on Owen's essay is in your gradebook, so you can answer my question.
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
Not in this meeting, Hale. Owen's zero: who decided, and when?
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
I'm not writing your email. You're writing about Owen's essay, and I'm still waiting. Who decided, and when?
